headline: Germany's far-right AfD scores landslide win in eastern state vote
description: The far-right Alternative for Germany won a landslide victory in Saxony-Anhalt state, located in the ex-communist east, taking at least 44% of the vote according to exit polls by two public broadcasters. But it is too early to tell whether they will have enough votes for an absolute majority to govern the state alone.

headline: The end of a lawless paradise? Local government seeks to take back control of Corsican islet
description: Cavallo, a little gem of the Lavezzi archipelago, has always sparked envy. Once the scene of wild parties, it drew the international jet set before becoming a target for nationalists and organized crime groups. In June, the local government launched an offensive to regain control of the port and open the island up to tourists.

headline: Business is booming for social run clubs
description: The rapid rise of these informal urban running groups, which offer a range of free services, is being strongly driven by the running ecosystem, which sees them as potential consumers in a market that grew by 17% in France in 2025.

headline: The letters from two Ukrainian sisters: 'Stay in bed or take shelter elsewhere: a life-or-death decision'
description: Sasha and Olga Kurovska are two Ukrainian sisters, one lives in Kyiv, the other in Paris. Faced with Russian strikes on civilian infrastructure, Sasha admires her fellow citizens' determination to never give up, while Olga, fresh from a month-long stay in Ukraine, better understands her sister's reactions to the constant threat of bombing.

headline: Spanish fashion giant Mango: From small clothing shop to its founder's tragic death
description: In May, Jonathan Andic was arrested on suspicion of murdering his 71-year-old father, who fell to his death in a ravine in 2024. It was a shocking and tragic end for Isak Andic, a son of Turkish immigrants who turned a small second-hand clothing shop in Barcelona into a thriving textile empire over the course of nearly four decades.

description: Hezbollah, the Lebanese Shiite movement, downplayed the Israeli forces' capture of the Ali Taher hill on Thursday and denounced the maneuver as an electoral ploy by Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.
